note: Majority: Child Care and Protection Act, 2015 (Act No. 3 of 2015, Government Gazette No. 5744 of 29 May 2015, in force 30 January 2019 by GN 4/2019 as NamibLII lists it), section 10: a person attains majority at 18 (it repealed the Age of Majority Act, 1957). Read in the Gazette copy archive.gazettes.africa holds. Work: Labour Act, 2007 (Act No. 11 of 2007), section 3(2): a person must not employ a child under 14; from 14 to 16 and to 18, further restrictions apply (section 3(3), not read whole). The Act was read only in NamibLII's own search results (its full page sits behind a Cloudflare challenge, not passed). For performers, section 234(2)(c) of the 2015 Act says that a child's taking part in an income-generating performance, display, activity, contest or event for advertising, beauty, sport, educational, religious, traditional, cultural or artistic purposes is not employment under section 3 of the Labour Act if a licence is first obtained from a children's commissioner, under regulations, with a parent's, guardian's or care-giver's written consent (not where a local or regional council has authorised the activity, and not for events the Minister's regulations prohibit). No lower age for the licence is set in the section; the 2019 regulations weren't read. Service: not read; no Namibian law calling anyone to military service was reached. Until 2026-11-03 NamibLII's search excerpt for the Labour Act was cited as primary; it is a legal information institute's copy of the law, so secondary since the ruling of 2026-11-03, so it was relabelled, and the Act was read that day in Gazette No. 3971's own pages (Laws.Africa's publication scan): s. 3(2) says a person must not employ a child under 14, so work stays from 14.

sources.title: Government Gazette of the Republic of Namibia No. 5744, 29 May 2015: Child Care and Protection Act, 2015 (Act No. 3 of 2015)
sources.said: 10. (1) A person attains the age of majority on attaining the age of 18 years. ... (2) It is not considered employment for the purposes of section 3 of the Labour Act, 2007 (Act No. 11 of 2007) for a person to use, procure, offer, employ, allow, induce or encourage a child to participate in ... (c) any performance, display, activity, contest or event for advertising, beauty, sport, educational, religious, traditional, cultural or artistic purposes, that is in any way intended to, used to or does generate income for any person or entity ... if - (i) prior to any child’s participation, a licence is obtained from a children’s commissioner

sources.title: NamibLII search results: Labour Act, 2007 (Act No. 11 of 2007), section 3 (excerpt)
sources.said: 3. Prohibition and restriction of child labour [...] prohibited in terms of this section. (2) A person must not employ a child under ... the age of 14 years.

sources.title: Government Gazette of the Republic of Namibia No. 3971, 31 December 2007: Labour Act, 2007 (Act No. 11 of 2007), s. 3 (the gazette's own pages, as Laws.Africa's publication scan holds them)
sources.said: Prohibition and restriction of child labour 3. (1) A person must not employ or require or permit a child to work in any circumstances prohibited in terms of this section. (2) A person must not employ a child under the age of 14 years.
